config-schema.rule: tokenguard config keys are declared in extension.json config_schema with x-sox-prompt + x-sox-default and additionalProperties:false; the running service reads them ONLY via SOX_CONFIG_<KEY> env (never a bespoke config-file reader) — same standardized path memory-server uses.

run-service-spec.rule: the unified service model still writes the registry.json entry shape {id,command,args,env,cwd,status,storePath}; http/stdio transports both register through run-service so the supervisor reads one registry — no parallel service registry is introduced.

supervisor-stop.rule: every supervised service (incl. the http port-holder) stops via SIGTERM then SIGKILL after stop_timeout_ms; tokenguard must terminate cleanly with zero orphan processes and release its port.

born-conformant-template.rule: serviceTemplate emits a born-conformant fileset (extension.json + package.json + tsconfig.json + src/index.ts + dist stub + CHANGELOG.md + README.md) so `sox init service` -> build -> validate passes with zero manual edits, by analogy to mcpServerTemplate.

host-keyed-target.rule: the service template emits NO literal host path (.claude/, ~/.claude.json); host-registry resolves the install target at install time, so the install descriptor stays host-agnostic.

c7-no-reach-in.rule: the tokenguard service imports the engine via the @sox/tokenguard-core package scope only — no cross-package ../dist reach-in (static or dynamic); enforced by @nx/enforce-module-boundaries + the C7 lint rule.

c6-policy-guard.rule: the tokenguard service enforces its declared permissions at the resource sink — it reads SOX_POLICY_* and denies a capture-dir write or upstream connection outside the declared fs/network allowlist BEFORE the side effect, mirroring memory-server's C6 guard.
